readmeExcerpt:
# Moonshine Voice

**Voice Interfaces for Everyone**

[Moonshine](https://moonshine.ai) Voice is an open source AI toolkit for developers building real-time voice agents and applications.

Full guides, models, and API reference are at **[moonshine-voice.readthedocs.io](https://moonshine-voice.readthedocs.io/)**.

- Everything runs on-device — fast, private, and with no account or API keys.
- Optimized for live streaming, with low latency by doing work while the user is still talking.
- Speech to text models trained from scratch, from [higher accuracy than Whisper Large V3](https://huggingface.co/spaces/hf-audio/open_asr_leaderboard) down to [tiny 1MB models](micro/README.md).
- One library across [Python, JavaScript/WASM, iOS, Android, macOS, Linux, Windows, and Raspberry Pi](https://moonshine-voice.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart/).

## Quickstart


```bash
pip install moonshine-voice
moonshine-voice mic --language en
```

Every other platform is covered in the [Quickstart](https://moonshine-voice.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart/), with runnable samples in [Examples](https://moonshine-voice.readthedocs.io/en/latest/examples/).

Building with a coding agent? Copy [`.agents/skills/moonshine-voice/`](https://github.com/moonshine-ai/moonshine/tree/main/.agents/skills/moonshine-voice) into your project's `.agents/skills/` folder, or run `npx skills add moonshine-ai/moonshine --skill moonshine-voice`. The skill teaches the current API shape so the agent does not reach for Whisper or the old `DialogFlow` names.

## Documentation

- [Quickstart](https://moonshine-voice.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart/) to install and run on your platform.
- [Using the Library](https://moonshine-voice.readthedocs.io/en/latest/using/) for transcription, text to speech, and conversational agents.
- [Models](https://moonshine-voice.readthedocs.io/en/latest/models/) for what's available, accuracy, and domain customization.
- [API Reference](https://moonshine-voice.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/classes/) for the classes, options, and C API.

## Support

- [Discord](https://discord.gg/27qp9zSRXF) for live support.
- [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/moonshine-ai/moonshine/issues) for bugs and feature requests.

## License

Licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). The models are MIT by default too, in every language and at every size — the only exceptions are the legacy non-streaming models for languages other than English, which stay under the non-commercial Moonshine Community License and are enumerated in [LICENSE](LICENSE).

aiSummary.oneLiner: A fast, cross-platform family of open speech-to-text models designed specifically for low-latency live voice interfaces.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Moonshine offers a suite of highly optimized speech-to-text (STT) and text-to-speech (TTS) models tailored for real-time applications. Unlike Whisper, which relies on fixed 30-second processing windows and recomputes from scratch, Moonshine utilizes an efficient streaming architecture that dynamically processes audio with caching to eliminate redundant computations. This approach achieves latencies often 5x lower than Whisper, making it suitable for live interactions and resource-constrained edge devices. It provides pre-built libraries and native examples across a wide array of platforms including iOS, Android, Linux, macOS, Windows, and Raspberry Pi, while offering multi-language support.
keyFeatures: Dynamic input windowing: Processes audio without the rigid 30-second constraints of Whisper, significantly cutting down wasted computation on short phrases.
State caching: Reuses previous computations during streaming audio input to ensure near-instant feedback for live voice interfaces.
Cross-platform edge support: Ships with self-contained, prebuilt libraries and starter projects for iOS, Android, Raspberry Pi, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
Multi-language availability: Supports languages including English, Spanish, Mandarin, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Ukrainian, and Arabic natively.
Variable model sizes: Offers Tiny, Small, and Medium streaming variants to allow developers to trade off parameter count (34M to 245M) for speed versus accuracy.

useCases.title: On-device transcription
useCases.description: Mobile engineers build offline dictation apps for iOS and Android using the provided lightweight C++ native libraries.

useCases.title: IoT and embedded systems
useCases.description: Makers and roboticists integrate Moonshine onto Raspberry Pi devices using the optimized Python package to handle voice commands offline.

useCases.title: Desktop dictation tools
useCases.description: Windows and macOS application developers implement continuous speech recognition without incurring cloud API costs or data privacy concerns.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Moonshine is built for developers, roboticists, and mobile engineers who need to integrate responsive, offline speech recognition and synthesis into applications where Whisper's latency or edge platform fragmentation is a bottleneck.
